title: Console feature activation runbook: dashboards, rollouts, and cost visibility training
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Overview: This ticket is the canonical activation runbook for three coordinated Console UX features landing in console-2026.04: (1) Dashboard Widgets v1.2 (configurable widget sizing + saved views), (2) Route Rollouts: canary + auto-fallback controls for model routing, and (3) Model Cost Breakdown: per-route token cost attribution and top-n expensive requests. Goal: enable a predictable, low-friction launch across Eng, Design, Docs, Support, Growth, and Sales, with training artifacts and release-note copy ready for customer-facing comms. Scope: final release notes, staged rollout schedule, internal playbook for on-call and CSMs, public changelog copy, training sessions (recorded + live Q&A), and in-console contextual help flows. Out of scope: API contract changes (handled under ENG-4982) and Dedicated billing reconciliation (tracked in PM-21900). Launch checklist (high level): 1) Finalize UX copy and help tooltips (owner: Design) 2) Lock code branch and merge release PRs (owner: Eng) 3) Smoke test rollout policy matrix in staging (owner: Eng/Reliability) 4) Produce internal runbook for Support & SRE (owner: PM) 5) Create CSM enablement deck and short demo script (owner: Growth/PM) 6) Schedule and record two 45-minute training sessions (owner: PM) 7) Publish release notes + changelog + in-console tooltip rollout (owner: Docs/Frontend) 8) Begin 7-day staged rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with canary heuristics and auto-fallback thresholds (owner: Eng/Platform) Responsibilities: - PM (Liam Chen): runbook owner, cross-team syncs, release notes copy, training scheduling - Engineering (ENG-4982 owner): rollout implementation, fallback rules, telemetry hooks - Design (DES-1347 owner): final UX text, microcopy, help panels - Docs (DOCS-88 owner): external release notes, API changelog, KB articles - Growth/CSM/Sales: customer comms, account outreach list, demo script - Support & SRE: incident playbook and on-call triggers Metrics and success criteria: - 95% of rollout users see stable latency within SLO range after full rollout - <0.5% increase in error rate attributable to rollout - 80%+ internal attendee completion of training or watched recording within first week - Post-launch feedback score from CSMs >= 4/5 - Reduction in cost-per-token variance for top 10 routes by 10% over 30 days Rollout strategy: staged canary with automated telemetry gates. Initial 10% traffic for 48 hours with active monitoring dashboards. If token-latency 95th percentile or error-rate delta exceeds threshold, auto-fallback triggers to previous routing policy. Canary groups will be selected to include both low- and high-throughput customers. Training plan: two live sessions (Americas and EMEA-friendly times), each recorded and accompanied by a 12-slide enablement deck, two short demo videos (2-3 minutes each) for embed in help center, and a one-pager 'What to expect' for CSMs. Training owners: Liam Chen (PM), Maria Gonzalez (Growth). Comms plan: 1) Internal: announcement in #console-prod two days before rollout, runbook link, SRE on-call schedule; 2) External: staged changelog post, email targeted to accounts that opt-in for early access, blog post highlighting cost visibility improvements after GA. Release notes (public): "Release highlights (console-2026.04): Configurable dashboard widgets for personalized monitoring, controllable route rollouts with canary + auto-fallback, and a new Model Cost Breakdown panel to help teams identify high-cost routes and optimize prompts. See the docs for migration steps and tips." Risks & mitigations: - Risk: hidden API regressions cause incorrect cost attribution. Mitigation: run synthetic traffic test harness and cross-validate cost numbers with billing team pre-GA. - Risk: support load spike when customers see new UI. Mitigation: pre-seed KB with troubleshooting steps and run two office-hours sessions in first week. Decisions / trade-offs: - Decided to ship Model Cost Breakdown without per-user labels in v1 to accelerate launch; will add in v1.1. Reason: per-user tagging requires billing changes and extended Q/A. - Chose staged rollout rather than feature flag per-account to simplify monitoring instrumentation. notes_for_on_call: On-call SRE should watch dashboard: rollout-canary-telemetry, model-cost-anomalies, route-error-delta. Trigger playbook if 95p latency increases >20ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows or error-rate delta >0.5%. Fallback policy: revert to previous routing policy and open incident with tag 'console-rollout'.
post_launch_followups: 1) Capture feedback in #console-feedback channel and summarize top issues within 72 hours. 2) Release v1.1 backlog for per-user cost tagging requested by Sales. 3) Evaluate telemetry for longer-term cost attribution accuracy and billing alignment (coord with billing team).
